Similarly, the VPs for round 6 do not add up to 8 because
Steve withdrew, much to the annoyance of John].

This was a 6-player game, and just about as good as jyhad games get. When
i started my final turn, i had ONE pool left. Two vampires got burned in
combat - one of michael's, by mark, and one of steve's by Bleu. Bleu by
the way was suffering from jet-lag and STILL put up a pretty scary
performance. As usual with my deck it was Kendrick with AUS and superior
Pulse who was the ultimate game-winner for me. Nice game, and looking
forward immensely to saturday for the sealed-deck tournament!

A couple of rules questions came up during this game, to which i don't
REALLY know the answers.

[1] Was it ok for Alex to use demonstration to cancel my Priscus's vote
during the college vote, thus allowing Steve to vote 3 with him? We
thought yes.

[2] Does Alvaro untap after successfully calling a vote, even if the vote
fails? We thought no. Except for Bleu, who invented the scheme.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
legb...@my-deja.com wrote:
> A couple of rules questions came up during this game, to
> which i don't REALLY know the answers.
>
> [1] Was it ok for Alex to use demonstration to cancel my
> Priscus's vote during the college vote, thus allowing Steve
> to vote 3 with him? We thought yes.

Correct.

If a vampire has his votes cancelled, he loses his vote(s), if
any, in both the Prisci subreferendum as well as his vote(s),
if any, in the main referendum.

> [2] Does Alvaro untap after successfully calling a vote,
> even if the vote fails? We thought no. Except for Bleu, who
> invented the scheme.

Alvaro gets blood when he abstains.

Perhaps you are thinking of Antonio:

Antonio Delgado [SAB] - Vampire (Las) (9)

* Antonio Delgado does not untap if the referendum isn't
successful (doesn't pass). [LSJ 19970224]
